tb21_profile.skill: Reverse the XOR encryption of a SQLite WAL file and hand-parse the WAL binary format (header/frames) to replay it and recover every record, emitting sorted JSON
tb21_profile.domain: SQLite internals and the write-ahead-log file format, binary file parsing, XOR/simple-cipher decryption, database recovery
tb21_profile.task_form: Recover/repair-corrupted-data: fix a broken binary WAL and reconstruct the full dataset that a naive reader misses

searches: tools.py search all "struct.unpack|parse the binary|binary format|hexdump|byte offset" -n 14

notes: TMax is overwhelmingly the right pool: it contains a large 'crashed DB, corrupted WAL, recover the records' family, several of which hand-parse a binary WAL (magic + length-prefixed frames) exactly like the TB task, and one (task_002461) that recovers a real orphaned SQLite .db-wal. final_top10 is 9/10 TMax by honest merit. The RTS and TerminalWorld shortlists were dominated by SQLAlchemy DB-init chores and Chinook table extraction (boilerplate, discarded); their real signal is the blkar/SBX corrupt-and-repair family and layered decode/decrypt chains, which match the repair-corrupted-data and decrypt-then-read shape but not SQLite/WAL specifically. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench can't match task_form (issue-fix); their best skill bridges are binary-format parsing - cantools bit/byte decode and especially SWE-Rebench's pfp (a binary-template parser) - plus the SQLite-backed libraries pudo/dataset and MonkeyType; scores kept honest at 2-3. Merge note: the blkar/SBX corrupt-repair seed appears in BOTH RTS (rts_task_a44e26e5, 0bdfa5f3, 25559b99) and TerminalWorld (tw_240491, tw_256057), so those picks are siblings; likewise several TMax WAL tasks share the '3 AM on-call, WAL won't replay' template but are genuinely distinct parsers.
